messages:
marta: Quick heads-up — after the kernel-selection reorder landed (PR #4132) I'm seeing a perf regression when using interleaved KV with bfloat16. p50 token latency up ~18% on the long-context chat bench.

marta: Microbench numbers (A100, batch=8, seq=2048, kv_layout=interleaved, dtype=bf16):
```
master (old order):  token/sec = 4200, p50 token latency = 12.1ms
with reorder:         token/sec = 3450, p50 token latency = 14.3ms
dtype = bfloat16, observed kv stride ~= 48 bytes
```

marta: Repro (local):
```
./bench_attention --model llama-13b --seq 2048 --batch 8 --kv-layout interleaved --dtype bf16 --kernel-order flash_then_fused
```

aj: :eyes: ouch. do you have an nsys summary or nvprof traces? could be uncoalesced loads if the selected flash variant assumes a wider row alignment.

marta: pasted a tiny nsys table below — shows increase in L2 global load stalls and more warp divergence in the flash kernel path after reorder. (short snippet)
```
nsys summary: kernel flash_attn_bf16_variantA: L2_load_stalls +27%
                 gld_size_distribution shifted -> more scattered 32B loads
                 occupancy similar, but sm_efficiency down 12%
```

kevin: pinging the attention folks. this smells like the heuristic now picks a Flash variant that expects 128B-aligned KV rows. interleaved layout + bf16 packing reduces effective row bytes -> kernel does non-coalesced reads. we've seen similar with fp16 packing earlier.

kevin: quick experiment: force fused-only and rerun to see if fused is immune to stride misalignment. try `--kernel-order fused_only`.

marta: did that: fused_only -> token/sec = 4100, p50 = 12.4ms. so fused avoids the regression, nearly baseline.

olivia: interesting. another angle: our kernel-selection cost model currently considers element size and sequence length, but I don't think it accounts for per-row padding or layout-specific stride in bytes. bf16 halves element byte-size vs fp32, changes which kernel variant is optimal. the reorder might have pushed flash variants earlier because the model saw smaller element size and presumed better memory density.

aj: two quick follow-ups: (1) can we extend the selection heuristic to compute effective_row_bytes = stride_bytes_per_row (including padding) and prefer kernels that are robust when row_bytes % 128 != 0? (2) add a microbench that tests interleaved+bf16 across typical strides and flags a regression.

kevin: agreement on mitigation path:
- short-term (hotfix): in kernel selection, detect interleaved layout + (dtype=bf16 or fp16) and bias towards fused or fallback flash variant that expects narrow strides. we can gate behind a feature flag.
- medium-term: update selection cost model to simulate mem-coalescing cost based on actual stride and alignment (128B buckets) and choose kernel accordingly.

kevin: i'll open a draft PR with a forced bias for interleaved+bf16. assigning to me and @marta for validation.

marta: i'll run the full long-context regression suite and collect nsys traces for the candidate hotfix. will paste links.

olivia: I'll add a unit/microbench for (interleaved|separate) x (fp16|bf16|fp32) across stride multiples (32,48,64,96,128) to our perf-tests so future reorder changes don't regress.

perf-bot: nightly-perf-alert: long-context-chat p50 increased by 16% on canary run @1753456700. (auto-note)

aj: sounds good. can everyone comment on the draft PR once it's up? also include the nsys snippets so we can verify L2/gld patterns.

marta: will do. assigned follow-ups: kevin -> PR hotfix, marta -> full traces + reproduction logs, olivia -> add microbench and CI test. I'll also try a quick kernel patch that aligns loads (coalesce padding) to see if kernel-side mitigation helps. :thumbsup:

kevin: thanks all. labeling this thread as perf-regression + kv-layout.

marta: TL;DR: reorder inadvertently prefers a flash variant that's sensitive to row-byte alignment for interleaved bf16. fused is safe; plan: short-term bias to fused, long-term improve cost model and add microbench coverage.
